channels_researched.name: National Taco Day date-error sweep (iLoyal.com, tripleseat.com, Fooda, Digital Hygge, Backyard Taco, and ~10 large aggregators)
channels_researched.status: genuine error found on iLoyal.com but channel + timing too weak to send — not pursued this round
channels_researched.notes: DayAlmanac's own national-taco-day page documents that National Day Calendar and Taco Bell jointly moved the observance off the fixed October 4 date to 'first Tuesday of October' in September 2024, and that many secondary calendar sites still show the stale October 4 date. Searched specifically for smaller (non-content-farm) sites still showing October 4 as current. iLoyal.com (a real Scottsdale, AZ marketing agency serving restaurants/bars, physical address + phone on file) published 'Holiday Marketing Calendar 2025 to 2026 for Restaurants and Bars' on 2025-10-21 listing 'Oct 4 National Taco Day' for their October 2025 section — which is wrong for 2025 too (the actual 2025 observance, per Taco Bell's own promotion, ran Tuesday Oct 7, 2025), and the article was published after that date had already passed, so the error is real but already stale for the reader. Site's post-sitemap shows genuine activity but with the most recent post from 2026-04-01 (about 4.5 months old, borderline against the 'last few months' bar), and no direct email was found anywhere on the site — only a phone number and a 'Master Support Form' meant for existing customers, not a fit channel for an unsolicited factual note. Checked tripleseat.com's food-holidays article (mentions National Taco Day with no specific date, nothing to correct), Fooda's 2026 food-days list (published 2026-08-05, does not list National Taco Day at all), Digital Hygge (correctly states the new first-Tuesday rule already), and Backyard Taco's blog post (stale, dated 2023-09-07). None of the large aggregators (National Today, Calendarr, WikiDates, AnyDayGuide, Awareness Days, CalendarLabs) were pursued as they are either direct competitors or content-farm-adjacent with no named editorial contact, consistent with prior rounds' findings on this class of site.

channels_researched.notes: DayAlmanac's own /virgo-dates/ page (highest-impression page in GSC, 1697 impr/28d) documents a genuine differentiated angle: tropical astrology's Aug 23-Sep 22 range shifts by a day some years due to equinox drift, a nuance essentially no astrology publisher mentions. But none of Britannica/AstroStyle/Horoscope.com/Astrology.com/Farmers' Almanac state anything factually wrong, just incomplete — there's no 'error' to correct, only a 'your page could be more precise' pitch, which is a much weaker angle than the date-correction pattern that has worked twice before. These are also all large, well-resourced publishers unlikely to respond to unsolicited small-site outreach. Not pursued this round; worth revisiting if a smaller astrology blog is found stating the date range as if it never moves.

channels_researched.status: not pursued — no error found, all sources agree on October 16, 2026
channels_researched.notes: Checked whether the 'moves to nearest weekday if Oct 16 falls on a weekend' rule was being misapplied anywhere (a plausible trap similar to the Grandparents Day/Labor Day pattern that worked before), since Oct 16, 2026 is a Friday and wouldn't trigger the adjustment. channels_researched.status: viable — pitch drafted, pending independent review, not yet sent
channels_researched.notes: wdea.am (a real Bangor/Downeast Maine AM radio station's blog) has a September 2023 personal post about National Sons Day, but it already acknowledges both dates casually ('There's also a National Sons Day on March 4th. Why are there 2? I don't know') — nothing to correct, and it's a stale 3-year-old post, not pursued. riyabhorkar.com (Riya's Blogs), a real actively-maintained personal creative-writing/lifestyle site (WordPress sitemap shows posts through July 2026, full site structure, named author with contact page), has a National Sons Day post that states the causality backwards: it calls September 28 'the widely accepted version' and March 4 'an older version that circulated online around 2018-2020,' when it's the reverse — March 4 has the named founder (Jill Nico, 2018) and registry backing (National Day Calendar, Checkiday), September 28 has no traceable origin per Checkiday founder Seth Westphal's own 2022 research. Drafted a factual correction pitch citing DayAlmanac's national-sons-day page. See outreach-drafts.md 2026-08-20 entry for full text.

actions_taken: No email sent, no form submitted this run (drafting only, per task rules — a separate step reviews and sends). Verified two previously-sent pitches (Keep Indiana Learning 2026-08-06, icalendars.net 2026-08-09) against their live pages: both classified published_no_link (neither correction was applied, no backlink added, dataforseo backlink check returned 0 total backlinks for dayalmanac.com). result_summary: 1/3 new topic angles produced a viable candidate this round. Step B verification (new this run) came back negative both times: neither prior date-correction pitch (Keep Indiana Learning, icalendars.net) resulted in the correction being applied or a backlink being added, roughly 2 weeks and 11 days after sending respectively, and dataforseo confirms dayalmanac.com currently has zero total backlinks recorded. This doesn't necessarily mean the pitches failed permanently (small independent sites/blogs often take longer than 2 weeks to action an email, if they act at all), but it's the first real data point on this outreach pattern's actual conversion rate: 0/2 converted so far, consistent with the low-single-digit-percent benchmarks documented in 独立站/外链外联真实案例调研.md rather than anything worse. The Riya's Blogs draft follows the same date-correction pattern that has now been used three times (Keep Indiana Learning, icalendars.net, Riya's Blogs) since it's the only angle that has gotten a real human response in this niche so far (the Keep Indiana Learning email did get a reply, per the 2026-08-06 log, even though the correction hasn't been applied to the post's new URL yet). GSC data continues to show the site is very early-stage (11 clicks, 7366 impressions over 28 days), which keeps outreach targets skewed toward small/personal blogs willing to respond to a cold, unbranded small site rather than large publishers.
